description: A rule line in five true Figma variant axes — Orientation, Style, Size, Color, and State — all directly switchable, matching how every other component in this file exposes its options.

mapping.note: States: Default → default, Hover → :hover (CSS), Focused → :focus (CSS), Selected → state="selected", Disabled → disabled

notes: Generated with the generic template: visuals come from Figma; keyboard, focus and ARIA behaviour are not specified.
A focus style exists in Figma, but the generic element is not focusable; it shows only when forced (data-force-state="focus") until behaviour is specified.

paragraphs: A rule line in five true Figma variant axes — Orientation, Style, Size, Color, and State — all directly switchable, matching how every other component in this file exposes its options.

sections.heading: Anatomy
paragraphs: ① Line — a single rectangle rendered via strokes only (never fills), for every Style value. Never a LINE node type, on either orientation.
Root is an auto-layout frame that hugs both axes at the Size-driven length (Sm=24px, Md=48px) and carries no fill of its own.

sections.heading: Variants & States
paragraphs: 540 variants total: Orientation(2) × Style(3) × Size(2) × Color(9) × State(5) — an owner-approved deviation from the 80-variant ceiling, so every combination stays directly selectable. Grid below is a deliberate representative subset: Color × Style at Orientation=Horizontal, Size=Md, State=Default. A mid-grey backdrop band is used since Light, Subtle, and Transparent are intentionally pale and would be invisible on plain white.

sections.heading: State — zoomed callout
paragraphs: Focused/Selected render at the strong stroke width (2px); Default/Hover/Disabled render at 1px — a difference easy to miss at grid thumbnail size. Shown here at Color=Dark, Style=Solid, Size=Md.

sections.heading: Token Map
paragraphs: component.divider collection (single value mode, 30 variables): 9 colour variables (each aliasing an existing semantic border token), 9 colour-opacity floats (0-100 scale — only Transparent is 0), 5 state stroke-width floats (Focused/Selected alias the 2px "strong" width, the rest alias 1px "default"), 5 state opacity floats (only Disabled is 40), 2 hug-length floats (Sm→24px, Md→48px).

sections.heading: Behaviour & Accessibility
paragraphs: Divider itself is not clickable — State is a visual signal set by the consumer, not user interaction. A List Item or Tabs component might instance a divider with State=Selected/Focused to draw a heavier, tinted line next to an active row/tab. Decorative — use role=separator when semantically meaningful, otherwise aria-hidden=true.

No gaps identified — the build matches the skill's 540-variant spec exactly, including the documented rectangle-thickness gotcha having been addressed (every variant binds both the length and thickness dimensions of its line rectangle).

No Do's/Don'ts section: the source skill's explicit rules (never use a LINE node, always bind both rectangle dimensions) are build-time instructions for whoever constructs the component, not consumer-facing usage guidance with a genuine visual counterexample — so none was fabricated here.

Variant grid shown is a deliberate 27-instance representative subset (Color × Style, 2 of 5 axes) rather than all 540 — reproducing the full matrix in one documentation frame was judged impractical; Orientation, Size, and State are demonstrated separately (State via the zoomed callout above).
